text: Every automatic payout in crypto has a catch: somebody still has to press the button. A savings goal fills up, and waits. An escrow is fully funded, and the freelancer still chases the release. GoalVault removes the button entirely.

GoalVault is a no-code builder for Reactive automations, built for the Set It and Forget It track. You pick a template: a savings goal, or pay-when-funded escrow, and the vault you deploy finishes itself. No code, no server, no keeper.

Creating one takes under a minute. Who should receive the money? What is the target? The dashboard turns plain answers into exact deployment parameters, and your wallet deploys the vault on Sepolia. Then you just fund it, whenever, in as many deposits as you like.

Behind the scenes, every deposit emits an event carrying the running total and the target. A reactive contract on Lasna listens for those events and checks the condition on-chain, in about a second. Below target, it does nothing. The moment the total reaches the target, it requests a callback: once, and only once.

The callback lands back on Sepolia and releases the funds to the beneficiary automatically. Here is a real goal from the live deployment: fully funded, one hundred percent, completed and paid out, with nobody pressing anything. The Reactive panel shows both automations live and subscribed.

And this is the proof, live on testnet. A deposit of zero point zero two ether crossed the zero point zero three target on Sepolia. The Lasna reactive transaction fired Goal Target Hit and requested the callback. One Sepolia block later, the callback transaction paid out the full amount. Both templates ran this exact loop, end to end.

It is also safe to leave running. A below-target deposit was evaluated and correctly ignored: zero logs, no payout. Contract debt is zero on both sides. Creators can cancel and refund every contributor, the owner can pause or retry a callback, and fifty-eight tests pass.
Set it, and forget it, because Reactive remembers for you. GoalVault: templates anyone can use, and automations that finish themselves. Thank you.
